selected_candidates.lesson_subject: NP7-offloaded GRE over software loopback: ECMP hashing, inner-header LAG distribution, and creation-time enablement
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: Directly relevant but older (2024-03-05): documents the control-plane/NP7 fast-path route-change discrepancy and the loopback-ecmp-offload remedy; used only as a troubleshooting scenario, not as the primary lesson source.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: NP7 GRE session fast-path ECMP over a software loopback; optional inner L3/L4 header inputs for LAG hashing through lag-hash-gre and NPU-GRE; loopback-ecmp-offload is a GRE-object creation-time choice.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create loopback and GRE tunnel with ECMP offload enabled -> route to remote GRE endpoint may change among underlay WANs -> NP7 hashes offloaded sessions across the available path set -> LAG may hash using inner packet headers -> verify actual egress distribution and offload behavior.
selected_candidates.failure_class: After underlay route change, initial software-forwarded packets use the new route but offloaded GRE traffic remains pinned to the old path or is unevenly distributed across LAG members.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Routing table shows new preferred route; uplink capture sees first packets on new WAN then later offloaded packets on old WAN; diagnose sys session list shows offload; tunnel creation config shows loopback-ecmp-offload; LAG config and NPU counters show hash distribution.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: On supported NP7/FortiOS builds create a replacement GRE tunnel with loopback-ecmp-offload enable (cannot be changed after creation); optionally set lag-hash-gre and aggregate algorithm NPU-GRE. On older releases, disable auto-asic-offload on the GRE policy as a throughput-costly workaround.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Underlay route preference changes from ISP1 to ISP2; first software packets move to ISP2 but established NP7-offloaded GRE packets continue on ISP1. Identify the creation-time tunnel option that enables ECMP hashing for loopback GRE offload.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two WAN underlay paths converge on FortiGate NP7; software loopback anchors GRE tunnel; NP7 offload path fans GRE sessions across ECMP next hops; inner L3/L4 header inputs feed LAG hash; remote GRE endpoint at far side.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: no prior lesson teaches NP7 GRE fast-path ECMP hashing or loopback-ecmp-offload. NAT64 and SD-WAN overlay provisioning share tunnel vocabulary but not the GRE hardware-hash mechanism.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiGuard package version pinning versus immediate downgrade for managed FortiGates
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched Community case verified in the rolling window. Community search did find an Oct 8 VDOM/ADOM deletion constraint, but it is outside the window and unrelated.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager acting as FortiGuard server selects the To Be Deployed Version for individual FortiGuard object packages; policy has two independent outcomes: freeze future delivery at the preferred version or actively downgrade devices already running later versions.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Device requests FortiGuard package -> FortiManager serves preferred package version instead of Latest -> administrator chooses Just Set Preferred Version or Downgrade -> device version state and future package eligibility diverge accordingly.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Signature/object behavior drifts after package update, or an administrator assumes selecting an older preferred version automatically rolls back devices when only the future delivery ceiling was changed.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiGuard > Packages > Receive Status shows current and To Be Deployed Version; managed-device table shows installed package versions; confirmation dialog distinguishes Just Set Preferred Version from Downgrade; subsequent package request behavior confirms the ceiling.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Search package with Show Used Objects Only cleared, select Change, choose version, then deliberately choose pin-only or immediate downgrade. Inventory the affected devices, confirm compatibility, and remember FortiManager retains at most 20 object versions by default.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A managed FortiGate is already on a newer application-signature package; operations wants to prevent future updates but does not want an immediate rollback. Choose the correct FortiManager action and predict the device state.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager FortiGuard package repository and preferred-version selector feed multiple managed FortiGates; a decision branch distinguishes version ceiling only from active downgrade of newer installed packages.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: security package version selection and rollback semantics are distinct from policy-package installation scheduling and ADOM schema upgrades.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: SNMPv3 monitoring and event traps for FortiAnalyzer system health
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: Related SNMP/MIB operational context from 2026-04-24, outside the 30-day window. It demonstrates per-ADOM MIB indexing, not the selected SNMPv3 trap-subscription workflow.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer system SNMP agent exposes queryable system information and emits event traps; SNMPv3 user security level independently controls authentication/privacy, query port and trap port, notification hosts, and selected event subscriptions; proprietary MIBs decode Fortinet OIDs.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable SNMP agent -> create SNMPv3 user with auth/no-privacy or auth+privacy -> configure notification hosts and SNMP event set -> SNMP manager polls on UDP/161 and receives traps on configured UDP/162 -> MIB database translates enterprise OIDs.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Monitoring polls work but traps are absent, or traps arrive but are undecodable/misinterpreted because user security, notification host, event selection, transport port, or MIB version is mismatched.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: SNMP agent enabled; v3 user security level and notification host list; query/trap status; manager-side authentication/packet capture; event-specific trap OID decoded using matching FORTINET-CORE and FortiAnalyzer MIBs.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable the agent; create an SNMPv3 user using SHA-family authentication and AES privacy where supported; enable queries/traps separately; add the manager as a notification host; select required events; load matching MIBs; test poll and trap paths independently.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A monitoring platform can poll FortiAnalyzer but receives no CPU/memory/log-disk notifications. Determine which SNMPv3 settings and evidence separate a successful GET path from trap delivery.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer SNMP agent at center; SNMP manager polling path on UDP/161 and asynchronous trap path on UDP/162; SNMPv3 user security envelope; MIB decoder on manager; event sources feeding trap selection.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: this is system-management SNMPv3 telemetry, not log forwarding, analytics, or FortiSwitch MAC-move traps.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiLink custom-command lifecycle: bind per-switch scripts and control on-replay versus on-any push timing
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched recent Community scenario verified. An Oct 14 VRRP route-monitor tip was found but is outside the window and unrelated.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiGate switch-controller stores generic FortiSwitch CLI commands, binds named custom commands to a managed-switch serial, and controls replay timing with switch-custom-cmd on-replay/on-any; bound commands are pushed last after controller-generated configuration.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Define command under switch-controller custom-command -> bind command-name under target managed-switch serial -> set global push mode -> any relevant managed-switch config change triggers a push under on-any -> controller applies standard config then executes custom command last.
selected_candidates.failure_class: A bound script appears in controller configuration but does not execute after a differential switch configuration update because the default on-replay mode waits for a full configuration replay; locally controlled settings may also overwrite an unbound one-time command.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: show switch-controller custom-command; managed-switch serial's config custom-command binding; switch-custom-cmd global value; controller push output showing command after other config; switch-side show/diagnostic confirms target setting.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Create the command with %0a line separators, bind it to the exact switch serial, set on-any when it must follow every configuration change, and verify the push output. Prefer binding over one-time execution for persistence; avoid commands whose settings are controller-owned unless the guide permits them.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A custom command is bound to a FortiSwitch, but a port VLAN change is pushed without the script. Identify the default push mode and the setting that executes bound commands after any switch configuration change.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate FortiLink controller -> managed-switch serial and command binding; configuration event -> standard switch config push -> custom command executes last; switch local state returns verification.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: controller script deployment timing is separate from clock, LACP, mirroring, and port QoS behavior.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Custom DHCP Option 82 construction per VAP: Circuit ID and Remote ID sub-options
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched Community troubleshooting scenario verified in the rolling window.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Wireless-controller VAP inserts DHCP relay-agent Option 82 metadata; Circuit ID can concatenate selected AP/SSID/VLAN/profile fields with a configurable delimiter, while Remote ID can carry client MAC; this is a VAP-level identity tag, not an IP address assignment mechanism.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client associates to VAP -> DHCP request traverses AP/bridge path -> FortiAP inserts configured Option 82 Circuit-ID/Remote-ID sub-options -> upstream DHCP server/policy uses those fields for scope or authorization -> DHCP reply returns to client.
selected_candidates.failure_class: DHCP server receives requests but cannot distinguish AP, SSID, VLAN, or client because Option 82 insertion is disabled, the wrong sub-options are selected, or the delimiter/expected server parser does not match.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: VAP configuration shows dhcp-option82-insertion and selected circuit/remote fields; WTP profile binds the VAP to radio; DHCP packet capture shows Option 82 sub-options and delimiter; server logs show received circuit/remote identifiers.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use FortiAP firmware 7.6.4 or later; enable insertion on the VAP; select only the AP/SSID/VLAN/profile identifiers the DHCP policy expects; set a stable delimiter; include client MAC as Remote ID if needed; apply the VAP through a WTP profile and inspect a DHCP capture.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Wireless DHCP requests reach the server, but all users land in the same scope because the server cannot distinguish SSID and AP. Select the VAP-level Option 82 composition that exposes both AP/SSID context and client identity.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wireless station -> FortiAP radio/VAP -> DHCP request with Option 82 Circuit ID (AP/SSID/VLAN/profile) and Remote ID (client MAC) -> relay/underlay -> DHCP server scope policy.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: DHCP relay metadata insertion is distinct from radio channel management and Multi-Link Operation.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Nested group hierarchy as a directed acyclic graph: detect and remove reciprocal membership cycles
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: Relevant Community scenario dated 2026-10-09, outside the strict rolling window. Used only to ground the failure signature; the lesson's group model and operations are sourced from the Administration Guide.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC groups are typed containers that may contain same-type subgroups and feed host/user policies and roles; membership is a directed graph; reciprocal or self-referential active edges create unbounded recursive traversal during group-tree rendering.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create typed group -> add members or same-type subgroups -> resolve membership for UI/policy use -> group hierarchy traversal recursively expands descendants -> cycle causes repeated node traversal and stack exhaustion -> remove one offending edge and rebuild the hierarchy.
selected_candidates.failure_class: System > Groups returns HTTP 500/Load Groups Error while group count remains nonzero; recursive GroupActions processing terminates with java.lang.StackOverflowError due to a self-loop or reciprocal group membership.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Groups page shows count but no rows; browser request to GroupActions.jsp fails; output.master contains repeated getGroupJSONObjectFromNode calls; read-only bsc.GroupMember query identifies PARENT_ID=CHILD_ID or reciprocal active elementClass=11 edges.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use Group Member Of and Show Members to inspect hierarchy where possible; if the UI is broken, collect logs and use only the documented read-only SQL diagnostics via execute db-shell; remove one reciprocal/self edge through supported group administration or TAC-guided repair; reload Groups and validate policy references.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: The FortiNAC Groups page shows 691 groups but no rows, and output.master repeats recursive group-node calls before StackOverflowError. Identify the graph defect and the safest first diagnostic.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Directed group graph with Group A -> Group B and Group B -> Group A cycle; side panel shows recursive UI traversal and stack overflow; remediation removes one directed edge to produce an acyclic hierarchy.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: internal nested-group graph integrity is distinct from RADIUS group attributes, RADIUS logs, and dashboard evidence.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: MDM Device Ownership to Host Role mapping and downstream NAC policy selection
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched recent Community scenario verified. The October 8 checksum and October 2 Winbind tips were found but are outside the window and unrelated.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Optional Update Hosts Role setting maps the MDM record's Device Ownership value into FortiNAC Host Role; role override is restricted to hosts whose role is NAC-Default or unset; roles become User/Host Profile filters and can affect downstream access policy.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint is identified and MDM service connector retrieves its record -> ownership attribute is read -> FortiNAC updates Host Role only when current role is default/unassigned -> User/Host Profile matches the role -> endpoint compliance/network access policy determines enforcement.
selected_candidates.failure_class: MDM shows a corporate/personal ownership value but FortiNAC policy continues to treat the endpoint as default or assigns the wrong access profile because role override is disabled, the connector lacks ownership data, or a manually assigned non-default role blocks override.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: MDM service connector Update Hosts Role setting; Host View Host Role and Managed By MDM/OT fields; source MDM ownership value; profile match and resulting Network Access Policy/VLAN; connector Last Successful Poll.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable Update Hosts Role only on supported connectors; verify the MDM record contains a recognized ownership value and that the connector poll succeeded; clear an intentional stale non-default role if policy permits; confirm Host Role updates and the User/Host Profile match before testing VLAN/policy enforcement.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: An Intune-managed endpoint reports Corporate ownership, but FortiNAC still matches the NAC-Default profile. Determine the connector option, the non-default-role override boundary, and the correct evidence chain.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: MDM platform -> FortiNAC MDM service connector -> host record; Device Ownership maps to Host Role -> User/Host Profile -> Network Access Policy -> switch/VLAN enforcement; override gate protects manually assigned roles.
closest_prior_topics: 2026-11-09 FortiNAC MDM service connector polling and host registration
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: this lesson is attribute-to-role policy mapping, not connector polling fan-out or session accounting.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP proxy architecture for Azure Government upstream identity providers
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: The Community sweep found an Oct 19 Ansible backup/restore tip, within the window but unrelated to SAML federation; no matched recent SAML-proxy scenario was verified.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator acts as the SAML IdP presented to downstream service providers while proxying authentication to an upstream Azure Government tenant; this avoids the commercial Azure OAuth Graph endpoint limitation (graph.microsoft.com versus Azure Government graph.microsoft.us) and preserves a FAC-controlled federation boundary.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Browser reaches FAC SAML IdP/SP portal -> FAC selects the configured remote SAML proxy realm -> browser is redirected to upstream Azure Government IdP -> upstream authenticates user and returns assertion to FAC -> FAC maps identity/attributes and issues its own SAML assertion to the downstream SP.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Azure Government identity integration fails when a feature relies on FortiAuthenticator's Azure Directory OAuth source hardcoded to graph.microsoft.com, or when remote SAML metadata, realm binding, portal URL, or SP trust is inconsistent.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Remote SAML server type Proxy and imported upstream IdP metadata/certificate; realm user source; FAC SAML IdP portal and default certificate; browser redirect chain; assertion issuer/audience/NameID and FAC logs; OAuth documentation identifies unsupported graph.microsoft.us endpoint for Azure Government.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Do not configure Azure Government as the commercial Azure Directory OAuth source. Use FAC as SAML IdP proxy: configure the remote SAML server with current government-tenant metadata and certificate, bind a realm, enable the FAC SAML IdP portal, configure the downstream SP, and validate issuer/audience/NameID and group mapping end to end.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A GCC High tenant is selected as FortiAuthenticator's Azure Directory OAuth source, but group lookup fails because the endpoint is graph.microsoft.com. Choose the supported FAC federation architecture for Azure Government.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Browser -> FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP portal -> upstream Azure Government SAML IdP -> assertion back to FortiAuthenticator -> downstream SAML service provider; trust metadata/certificates at both federation edges.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: upstream Azure Government proxying is a distinct federation topology from per-SP group authorization and signing-certificate rotation.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Active Directory LDAP password reconciliation using a privileged reconcile secret
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched FortiPAM Community troubleshooting scenario verified in the rolling window.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A base account secret can use a separate privileged reconcile account as the bind identity for resetting the base password when it cannot change its own password or its stored password is out of sync; activation can be direct or only after a password-change failure; feature is limited to Active Directory LDAP password changers.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Password change/verification/check-in begins -> password changer attempts normal base-account password update -> configured activation condition determines whether reconciliation runs -> privileged reconcile secret binds to directory and resets base account password -> FortiPAM stores/validates the new secret value.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Password rotation or check-in fails because the base account lacks password-reset rights or FortiPAM's stored credential is already out of sync with Active Directory; a normal password change cannot recover the account.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Secret template password changer type is Active Directory LDAP; Password Reconciliation enabled; Reconcile Account reference; Activate on mode; password changer task result; target AD account state and FortiPAM Verify Password result.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Create a separate privileged AD account secret with only the required reset rights, reference it as Reconcile Account, choose Reconcile directly or Upon Password Change Failure based on the recovery policy, test against a controlled out-of-sync account, and verify the new password at both AD and FortiPAM.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: An AD service account's password is out of sync and the base account cannot reset its own password. Select the FortiPAM mechanism that uses a separate privileged bind identity and the appropriate activation point.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM base secret/password changer -> Active Directory LDAP target; separate privileged reconcile secret binds to AD and resets base account; manual/automatic/check-in triggers converge on reconciliation decision.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: reconciliation is a separate credential-recovery authority, not password verification or user lifecycle purging.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Analytics query functions: extraction, normalization, aggregation and moving averages
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched recent FortiSIEM Community query-function scenario verified in the rolling window.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM Analytics query expressions add EXTRACT, IF, string normalization, conversion, advanced aggregates, and SMA/EMA; engine and context scope differ—functions are available in ClickHouse/Elasticsearch queries, with nesting limits and no support for EventDB queries/rules as described in release notes.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select ClickHouse or Elasticsearch query -> filter raw events -> extract or normalize fields -> convert types/derive conditional values -> group and aggregate -> apply time-bucket SMA/EMA -> render result; unsupported engine/context rejects or omits function behavior.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Query errors or misleading results occur when a function is used in EventDB/rules, nesting exceeds engine-specific limits, EXTRACT pattern returns the wrong type, or SMA/EMA lacks a supported time aggregation field.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Query engine selected; function availability and nesting error; raw event field versus EXTRACT output; group-by and time-bucket fields; sample rows and result type; comparison against raw event data.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Run advanced function queries only in supported ClickHouse/Elasticsearch Analytics contexts; use EXTRACT for a single missing value from historical raw logs; normalize strings before grouping; convert numeric values explicitly; provide hourly/daily/weekly/monthly receive-time aggregation for EMA/SMA; keep nesting within documented engine limits.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A historical raw event contains an interface identifier embedded in a message, and the engineer needs a normalized per-hour trend. Choose the supported query engine and sequence of EXTRACT, string normalization, conversion, and EMA.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Raw event stream -> ClickHouse/Elasticsearch query engine -> EXTRACT/IF/string/conversion stage -> group-by aggregates -> time-bucket SMA/EMA -> Analytics output; EventDB/rules branch marked unsupported.
closest_prior_topics: 2026-11-10 FortiSIEM event aggregation and threshold-based incident rules
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: query expression capabilities and engine-specific function scope are distinct from incident rule aggregation and integrity checks.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiClient internet-reachability gate before FortiSASE VPN autoconnect
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched recent FortiSASE Community troubleshooting scenario verified in the rolling window.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Endpoint profile controls VPN autoconnect and Disable internet check; with the check enabled/setting left disabled, autoconnect waits until Internet connectivity is confirmed; enabling Disable internet check bypasses the readiness gate and starts autoconnect even when Internet is unavailable.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User logs in or endpoint profile triggers auto-connect -> FortiClient evaluates local Internet reachability unless the check is disabled -> when reachable, client initiates FortiSASE SIA/IPsec tunnel -> authentication and PoP connection proceed; bypass mode attempts tunnel initiation without the precheck.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Tunnel appears not to start on a captive-portal/offline network when the Internet check gate is active, or clients repeatedly attempt a tunnel before local Internet connectivity when the gate is disabled.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Endpoint profile Connection tab shows automatic/manual mode and Disable internet check state; endpoint local connectivity test; FortiClient connection log timestamps relative to network readiness; SASE tunnel/authentication logs distinguish precheck from post-connect failure.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Keep Disable internet check off for normal connectivity-gated autoconnect; use manual connection when the user must complete captive-portal onboarding; enable the bypass only for a deliberate deployment that needs an immediate tunnel attempt; verify profile assignment and endpoint behavior.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A laptop on hotel Wi-Fi starts repeated FortiSASE tunnel attempts before the captive portal has granted Internet access. Identify the endpoint-profile toggle that bypasses the pre-connectivity gate.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint/FortiClient -> Internet reachability decision gate -> FortiSASE SIA tunnel -> Security PoP; bypass branch skips the gate and attempts tunnel establishment while offline.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: local Internet readiness gating precedes tunnel establishment; it is distinct from pre-logon authentication and DPD keepalive behavior.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Traffic-class assignment and guaranteed bandwidth for SD-WAN performance SLA probes
selected_candidates.scenario_relation: No directly matched recent Community scenario verified. The FortiGate community search found unrelated firmware-hardening material; the selected lesson is based on the current FortiOS 8.0 Administration Guide.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A health-check's class-id maps SLA probe packets into a firewall traffic-class and egress shaping-profile entry; configured priority and guaranteed-bandwidth percentage protect probes during congestion so health measurement does not falsely report a failed path because probes were starved.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Define traffic-class IDs -> map IDs in shaping-profile with priority/guaranteed/max bandwidth -> bind egress shaping profile and outbandwidth to participating interfaces -> assign class-id to SD-WAN health-check -> probe packets traverse the egress scheduler -> class counters and SLA metrics validate behavior.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Production traffic congestion starves low-priority SLA probes, causing false packet loss/latency and unnecessary SD-WAN failover or link flapping even though the underlay is usable.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: health-check shows latency/loss; `diagnose netlink interface list` displays class bandwidth allocation, priority and counters; class counter increments for the probe class; `diagnose sys sdwan health-check` confirms probe state and measured metrics.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Create a dedicated traffic class, assign a high or medium priority and realistic guaranteed bandwidth in a shaping profile, attach it to each egress interface, set the health-check class-id, and verify the class counter increases under congestion. Do not give probes unbounded priority or confuse class-id with DSCP marking.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: During busy-hour egress congestion, SLA probes lose packets while user traffic remains usable, causing path flaps. Choose the class-id and shaping-profile mechanism that protects measurement traffic and the counter that proves it.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: SD-WAN health-check probe -> class-id mapping -> firewall traffic class -> egress shaping profile on each WAN member -> priority/guaranteed bandwidth scheduler -> WAN link; probe result returns to SLA member-selection logic.
closest_prior_topics: 2026-11-17 Secure SD-WAN TWAMP Performance SLA probes
2026-11-03 Secure SD-WAN adaptive FEC using SLA metrics and DSCP
selected_candidates.uniqueness_decision: ACCEPT: this is egress scheduler protection for probe packets, not probe protocol selection, FEC adaptation, or measured-bandwidth shaping.
